To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 98-base repeat of the JCVE virus contains multiple regulatory elements that are recognized by glial cell nuclear proteins.

a novel transcription factor, designated glial origin protein, interacts with a specific cis-acting regulatory element within the JCVE promoter and positively regulates transcription of the JC virus in glial cells.

(1) a novel transcription factor, designated JBP45, is involved in the regulation of the JCVE viral promoter in brain cells, and (2) JBP45 interacts with the central region of the JCVE repeat and stimulates transcription of the viral promoter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the cellular factors that regulate the transcription of JCVE, the promoter for human neurotropic JC virus.
the identification of the molecular mechanism(s) involved in the cell type-specific regulation of JCVE transcription.
the molecular mechanisms that control the transcription of the human JCVE promoter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the novel glial-specific transcription factor is a brain-specific protein that interacts with the central domain of the 98-base repeat and stimulates the JCVE promoter.
the glial-origin transcriptional factor is a brain-specific protein that interacts with a cis-acting sequence in the JCVE promoter and increases transcriptional activity of this promoter in vitro.
the novel glial origin transcription factor is a brain-specific protein that binds to a specific site on the JCVE promoter and increases transcription of the promoter in non-glial cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glial-origin factor is a novel transcription factor that is involved in the activation of a human neurotropic JC virus promoter.
the glial-origin transcription factors are involved in cell type-specific transcription in glial and neuronal cells.
